name: WildNav
summary: Python pipeline that localizes a drone by matching its downward camera frames against georeferenced satellite map tiles with SuperGlue, then converts the best match into GPS coordinates. Companion code to the 'Vision-based GNSS-Free Localization for UAVs in the Wild' paper.
why_it_matters: The canonical small, readable reference for absolute visual localization over non-urban terrain - exactly the 'visual GPS' building block a GNSS-denied team needs.
hackathon_notes: Clone, drop in your own map tiles with corner coordinates and a few drone photos; runs on a laptop GPU. Brute-force tile search is slow - add a retrieval stage (AnyLoc/SALAD) to prune candidates.

name: visual_localization (GNSS-free UAV)
summary: A cleaner reimplementation of the WildNav idea: match UAV images to satellite tiles with SuperPoint/SuperGlue-style matchers and estimate geographic position.
why_it_matters: Packaged, modular take on the WildNav approach that is easier to extend with newer matchers.
hackathon_notes: Good starting skeleton if WildNav's scripts feel too ad hoc; swap the matcher for LightGlue or XFeat for speed.

name: UAVLocalization (map retrieval + alignment)
summary: Geo-localization system for aerial platforms that first retrieves the right satellite map region with a deep descriptor and then aligns the drone orthophoto to it to extract coordinates; evaluated on reorganized public AgEagle datasets and a field test.
why_it_matters: Shows the two-stage retrieve-then-align architecture end to end with field data, the design most practical systems converge on.
hackathon_notes: Use its pipeline layout as the backbone of a demo; datasets need a separate download. Conda env file provided.

name: AnyVisLoc benchmark
summary: Benchmark and code for UAV absolute visual localization under low-altitude, multi-view (oblique) observation, comparing retrieval and matching combinations against aerial and satellite reference maps.
why_it_matters: One of the most up-to-date (2025) systematic comparisons of what actually works for low-altitude drones, which is the regime of small tactical UAVs.
hackathon_notes: Read its results before choosing a retrieval/matcher combo; reuse its evaluation scripts to score your own pipeline.

name: U2S-CVGL (scale-aware UAV-to-satellite)
summary: Scale-aware cross-view geo-localization method for matching UAV views to satellite imagery when the altitude-driven scale difference is unknown.
why_it_matters: Scale mismatch is one of the main failure modes when flight altitude is uncertain; this targets it directly.
hackathon_notes: Research code; useful if your demo flies at varying altitudes and fixed-scale tiles break.

name: GNSS-Denied UAV Geolocalization (terrain-weighted)
summary: Code and demos for a UAV geolocalization system that combines image matching, visual odometry and a terrain-weighted constraint optimization, intended to work day and night.
why_it_matters: Fuses absolute map matches with relative VO and terrain constraints - the hybrid structure a real GNSS-denied nav stack needs.
hackathon_notes: Check what is actually released before planning around it; mainly a reference for the fusion design.

name: GeoAnchor
summary: Recent project fusing visual odometry with satellite-map matching in a particle filter for GNSS-denied UAV flight, with an explicit notion of when the map match should not be trusted; evaluated on UAV-VisLoc flights and with a browser demo.
why_it_matters: Directly addresses the practical problem that per-frame map matching often fails (water, farmland, repetitive texture), and shows how to bridge with VO.
hackathon_notes: Very recent single-author project; good blueprint for a 48h demo combining VO drift with intermittent absolute fixes. Verify numbers yourself.

name: KF-HomoVAL
summary: 6-DoF absolute visual localization for UAVs built on deep homography estimation between the drone view and a reference map, smoothed with a Kalman filter.
why_it_matters: Homography-based registration gives full pose, not just a location, which helps when the camera is not nadir.
hackathon_notes: Pair with the STHN family for comparison; expect to retrain on your imagery.

name: UAVision
summary: Map-matching-based visual localization software for UAVs in GNSS-denied settings, shipped with a GUI front end and demo.
why_it_matters: One of the few projects packaged as an operator-facing tool rather than a paper repo.
hackathon_notes: Useful for UI inspiration and a quick demo; inspect the matcher it uses before relying on accuracy.

name: Visual Locator
summary: Absolute drone positioning by image retrieval (SelaVPR-style ViT features) over cropped satellite tiles followed by registration with SIFT+RANSAC or SuperPoint+SuperGlue.
why_it_matters: Clean example of a retrieval + registration pipeline that compares classic and learned matchers side by side.
hackathon_notes: Training described used a multi-GPU server; for a hackathon reuse pretrained weights and the pipeline code only.

name: Aerial Template Matching
summary: Classical template-matching approach for locating an aerial image inside a larger reference image, built on OpenCV.
why_it_matters: A zero-training baseline to compare learned matchers against; mirrors classic DSMAC-style scene correlation in spirit.
hackathon_notes: Runs instantly; good as a fallback or ablation baseline in a demo.

name: CrossLoc
summary: CVPR 2022 cross-modal visual representation learning for absolute camera localization of aerial imagery, trained largely on synthetic data rendered from geodata.
why_it_matters: Shows that synthetic renders from DEM/orthophoto can train localizers for real flights - a cheap way to cover new terrain.
hackathon_notes: Older and heavy to set up; read for the synthetic-data idea.

name: JointLoc
summary: Real-time visual localization framework for planetary UAVs that jointly uses relative and absolute pose estimation against orbital maps.
why_it_matters: Planetary flight is the purest GNSS-free case; the joint relative+absolute design transfers to Earth.
hackathon_notes: C++ build; mostly a design reference.

name: University-1652 baseline
summary: Dataset and baseline code for drone-based geo-localization across drone, satellite and ground views of university buildings worldwide.
why_it_matters: The standard drone-to-satellite retrieval benchmark; most cross-view papers report on it.
hackathon_notes: Dataset requires a request form; the synthetic drone views are building-centric, not wide-area terrain.

name: SUES-200 benchmark
summary: Multi-height, multi-scene drone-satellite cross-view dataset and evaluation code, capturing drone imagery at several altitudes.
why_it_matters: Adds altitude variation that University-1652 lacks - closer to real flight profiles.
hackathon_notes: Use as a second evaluation set alongside University-1652.

name: DenseUAV
summary: Dataset and baseline (TIP 2023) for UAV self-positioning in low-altitude urban environments using dense sampling of drone and satellite views.
why_it_matters: Targets self-positioning (where am I) rather than target retrieval, with dense reference sampling.
hackathon_notes: Good dataset for training a retrieval head for urban flights.

name: Sample4Geo
summary: Cross-view geo-localization training with hard negative sampling, reporting strong results on drone-satellite and street-satellite benchmarks with a simple contrastive setup.
why_it_matters: A strong, simple baseline that is easy to retrain for your own drone/satellite pairs.
hackathon_notes: Pretrained checkpoints help; fine-tune on your tile set if time allows.

name: LPN (Local Pattern Network)
summary: PyTorch implementation of a cross-view geo-localization method that pools features in rings around the image center to capture contextual local patterns.
why_it_matters: Widely used baseline in drone-satellite retrieval; useful to understand rotation-robust pooling.
hackathon_notes: Mainly as a comparison baseline.

name: UAV-VisLoc dataset
summary: Large-scale dataset of real UAV flight imagery with satellite reference maps for UAV visual localization across varied terrain.
why_it_matters: Real nadir-ish drone frames with ground truth over large, non-urban areas - the closest public match to a GNSS-denied flight test.
hackathon_notes: Best dataset to test a visual-GPS demo; pick one flight and its map, run your matcher, plot error vs ground truth.

name: Satellite-thermal geo-localization
summary: IROS 2023 code for long-range UAV thermal geo-localization against satellite RGB imagery, using domain adaptation to bridge thermal and visible imagery; comes with the Boson-nighttime dataset.
why_it_matters: Night flight is when GNSS-denied UAVs are most exposed; this is the main open line of work for thermal-to-satellite matching.
hackathon_notes: Dataset on Hugging Face (gated). Use the pretrained model to show night-time matching in a demo.

name: STHN
summary: Deep homography estimation for aligning UAV thermal images to satellite maps (RA-L 2024), refining coarse geo-localization into precise alignment.
why_it_matters: Turns a coarse thermal match into an accurate position fix.
hackathon_notes: Combine with the IROS 2023 retrieval stage from the same lab.

name: UASTHN
summary: ICRA 2025 extension of STHN that adds uncertainty estimation to satellite-thermal homography, so the system can say when a fix is unreliable.
why_it_matters: Calibrated uncertainty is what lets a nav filter safely ingest visual fixes.
hackathon_notes: Feed its uncertainty into your EKF measurement covariance.

name: SCC-Loc
summary: Zero-shot UAV thermal geo-localization against satellite imagery without thermal-specific training.
why_it_matters: Zero-shot avoids collecting paired thermal data, a common blocker.
hackathon_notes: Very recent; check release completeness.

name: Seasonally invariant transform (visual TRN)
summary: Training code for a learned image transform that makes aerial imagery robust to seasonal appearance change for visual terrain-relative navigation.
why_it_matters: Reference maps are often from a different season than the flight; this attacks that gap.
hackathon_notes: Older; reference for appearance-change preprocessing.

name: CELL
summary: Event camera localization in prior lidar maps with confidence weighting.
why_it_matters: Event cameras keep working in low light and fast motion, relevant for night localization against a prior map.
hackathon_notes: Requires event camera data; mostly a reference.

name: AnyLoc
summary: Universal visual place recognition using foundation-model (DINOv2) features with VLAD/GeM aggregation, working across aerial, underwater, indoor and outdoor domains without task-specific training.
why_it_matters: Training-free retrieval that already works on aerial imagery - the fastest way to get a coarse 'which tile am I over' stage.
hackathon_notes: Extract descriptors for your satellite tiles offline, query with drone frames; then refine with LightGlue/RoMa.

name: hloc
summary: Toolbox for hierarchical visual localization: global retrieval (NetVLAD etc.) to find candidate images, then local feature matching (SuperPoint, LightGlue...) and PnP against an SfM model.
why_it_matters: The standard plumbing for coarse-to-fine localization; ready-made wrappers for most retrieval and matching models.
hackathon_notes: Use its retrieval + matching APIs even without the SfM part; pip-installable.

name: EigenPlaces
summary: ICCV 2023 visual place recognition training method for viewpoint-robust descriptors.
why_it_matters: Viewpoint robustness matters when drone heading and tilt vary against nadir satellite tiles.
hackathon_notes: Pretrained models loadable via torch.hub.

name: CosPlace
summary: CVPR 2022 large-scale visual geo-localization treating place recognition as classification over geographic cells.
why_it_matters: Scales to very large maps, a useful framing for country-sized reference databases.
hackathon_notes: torch.hub weights available.

name: SALAD
summary: Place recognition descriptor using optimal-transport aggregation of DINOv2 features.
why_it_matters: Among the strongest off-the-shelf retrieval descriptors; good drop-in for the coarse stage.
hackathon_notes: Load via torch.hub, compare with AnyLoc on your tiles.

name: MixVPR
summary: WACV 2023 place recognition descriptor built by MLP feature mixing; lightweight and fast.
why_it_matters: Compact descriptors suit embedded retrieval on a drone.
hackathon_notes: Fast inference; good for an onboard-feasibility story.

name: BoQ
summary: CVPR 2024 place recognition with a bag of learnable global queries over backbone features.
why_it_matters: Recent strong retrieval model with simple usage.
hackathon_notes: torch.hub available.

name: SelaVPR
summary: ICLR 2024 method adapting pretrained foundation models for place recognition with lightweight adapters, producing both global and local features.
why_it_matters: Global+local output lets one model do retrieval and re-ranking.
hackathon_notes: Used by Visual-Locator for UAV retrieval.

name: VPR methods evaluation
summary: Wrapper exposing many state-of-the-art place recognition models behind one interface so you can switch models with one parameter.
why_it_matters: Fastest way to benchmark several retrieval models on your own drone/satellite set.
hackathon_notes: Point it at a folder of tiles and queries; compare recall in an hour.

name: LightGlue
summary: Fast learned local feature matcher (ICCV 2023) that adapts its depth to pair difficulty; works with SuperPoint, DISK, ALIKED and SIFT features.
why_it_matters: The default fine-matching stage for drone-to-tile registration today: accurate and fast enough for near-real-time.
hackathon_notes: pip install; use SuperPoint+LightGlue between a drone frame and top-k retrieved tiles, then RANSAC homography.

name: Glue Factory
summary: Training library for local feature detection and matching (trains LightGlue and others).
why_it_matters: Lets you fine-tune a matcher on aerial/satellite pairs if off-the-shelf models struggle.
hackathon_notes: Training takes longer than a hackathon; use for post-event work.

name: SuperGlue (pretrained)
summary: Pretrained SuperGlue graph-neural-network matcher with SuperPoint features (CVPR 2020).
why_it_matters: Used by WildNav and many UAV localization repos; non-commercial license limits reuse.
hackathon_notes: Prefer LightGlue (permissive license, faster) unless replicating WildNav exactly.

name: SuperPoint (pretrained)
summary: Pretrained SuperPoint keypoint detector and descriptor.
why_it_matters: Feature front end for SuperGlue/LightGlue pipelines.
hackathon_notes: Most users get SuperPoint via LightGlue/hloc now.

name: LoFTR
summary: Detector-free transformer matcher producing dense-ish correspondences, good on low-texture scenes.
why_it_matters: Low-texture terrain (fields, desert) breaks keypoint matchers; detector-free matching helps.
hackathon_notes: Also available in kornia for easy use.

name: RoMa
summary: Robust dense feature matcher (CVPR 2024) estimating pixel-dense warps with certainties, strong under large appearance change.
why_it_matters: Handles season, lighting and sensor differences between drone frames and satellite imagery better than sparse matchers, at higher compute cost.
hackathon_notes: Use as the accurate-but-slow verifier on the top retrieval hit; GPU recommended.

name: MASt3R
summary: Matching grounded in 3D: predicts dense correspondences and 3D pointmaps from image pairs, building on DUSt3R.
why_it_matters: Robust to extreme viewpoint change (oblique drone view vs nadir satellite) because it reasons in 3D.
hackathon_notes: Heavy model and non-commercial license; good for offline demos.

name: XFeat
summary: Lightweight local feature extractor and matcher (CVPR 2024) designed for speed on constrained hardware.
why_it_matters: Fits onboard compute on small drones where LightGlue on GPU is not available.
hackathon_notes: Runs on CPU in real time; good for an embedded/Jetson story.

name: vismatch (image-matching-models)
summary: Wrapper exposing 50+ image matching models behind one interface (formerly image-matching-models).
why_it_matters: Swap SIFT, LightGlue, LoFTR, RoMa, MASt3R etc. with one line to find the best matcher for your imagery.
hackathon_notes: Best first stop for matcher selection during the hackathon.

name: python-tercom
summary: Python demo of TERCOM terrain contour matching: simulate a radar-altimeter profile over a DEM and correlate it against the map to recover position.
why_it_matters: Smallest end-to-end TERCOM sim to understand and extend for a DEM-matching demo.
hackathon_notes: Load an SRTM/Copernicus DEM tile, generate a profile, show the correlation surface; an afternoon's work.

name: tercom_nav (TERCOM + ESKF)
summary: ROS 2 package combining TERCOM-style terrain matching with an error-state Kalman filter for UAV navigation.
why_it_matters: Bridges batch terrain matching into a recursive filter that a real autopilot stack could consume.
hackathon_notes: Good if your team runs ROS 2 with PX4/ArduPilot SITL; pair with a DEM and simulated altimeter.

name: TERCOM via particle filter
summary: MATLAB SIR particle filter estimating UAV position from terrain contour matching in GPS-denied flight.
why_it_matters: Particle filters handle the multimodal ambiguity of terrain matching better than a single correlation peak.
hackathon_notes: Port the filter loop to Python for a demo.

name: TERCOM-python (TERCOM + DSMAC)
summary: OpenCV-based demo of map-based navigation combining terrain contour matching with scene-matching area correlation.
why_it_matters: Shows both classic map-matching families side by side.
hackathon_notes: Small educational code; use for concept slides and quick baselines.

name: terrain-nav-preprocessing
summary: Preprocessing tools for terrain-referenced navigation, generating DEM tiles with controlled noise for training and evaluation.
why_it_matters: Saves time preparing DEM data for TRN experiments.
hackathon_notes: Use to build synthetic DEM test sets.

name: MagNav.jl
summary: Julia package from the DAF-MIT AI Accelerator for airborne magnetic anomaly navigation: flight/INS data import or simulation, anomaly maps, aircraft magnetic compensation (Tolles-Lawson and neural models) and navigation filters.
why_it_matters: The reference open toolkit for MagNav, with real flight data from the challenge problem; magnetic nav is unjammable by RF.
hackathon_notes: Install Julia and run the documented examples on the challenge flight data; compensation + EKF in a day.

name: MagNavPy
summary: Python port of MagNav.jl for magnetic navigation research.
why_it_matters: Lets Python-only teams use the MagNav workflow without learning Julia.
hackathon_notes: Community port; verify outputs against MagNav.jl examples.

name: MAMMAL
summary: Python package (Magnetic Anomaly Map Matching Airborne and Land) for simulating and processing aeromagnetic survey data and building anomaly maps for MagNav.
why_it_matters: Map creation is the hidden half of MagNav; this covers it in Python.
hackathon_notes: Use to generate maps or simulated surveys feeding a particle filter.

name: AFIT MagNav example data
summary: Sample data for MagNav work: MIT-AIA anomaly maps, a challenge flight, North American magnetic anomaly grids and geoid files.
why_it_matters: Ready-made data so a team can start without hunting for maps.
hackathon_notes: Grab these files first.

name: Rao-Blackwellized SLAM smoothing (magnetic)
summary: MATLAB code for Rao-Blackwellized particle smoothing for SLAM, including magnetic field mapping and map-matching localization with a magnetometer.
why_it_matters: Clean academic reference for magnetic field SLAM and particle-filter matching at small scale.
hackathon_notes: Good for understanding magnetic map matching quickly.

name: MagNav deep-learning compensation
summary: Deep-learning approach to aircraft magnetic disturbance compensation built around the MagNav challenge data.
why_it_matters: Compensation quality dominates MagNav accuracy; shows a learned alternative to Tolles-Lawson.
hackathon_notes: Notebooks run on challenge data.

name: DroneMagNav
summary: Open hardware + firmware design for a drone magnetic-anomaly navigation board (ESP32-S3, magnetometer, IMU, baro) running particle-filter matching against a global anomaly map and feeding position to a flight controller over MAVLink.
why_it_matters: Rare example of MagNav pushed down to cheap drone hardware with an autopilot interface.
hackathon_notes: Very recent single-author project; hardware not validated in flight per what we could see. Global anomaly maps are coarse, so expect km-level, not meter-level, results on small drones.

name: tetra3
summary: Fast lost-in-space plate solver for star trackers from ESA: identifies stars in an image and returns attitude using a precomputed pattern database.
why_it_matters: Star-based attitude (and with time + gravity vector, position) is jam-proof; tetra3 is the easiest open solver.
hackathon_notes: Not on PyPI: pip install git+https://github.com/esa/tetra3.git; solve sample images in minutes. Combine attitude with a level sensor and clock for a celestial fix demo.

name: cedar-solve
summary: Actively maintained fork of tetra3 with speed and robustness improvements, used in the Cedar telescope-aiming product.
why_it_matters: More maintained than upstream tetra3 for new work.
hackathon_notes: Drop-in alternative to tetra3.

name: OpenStarTracker
summary: Open-source star tracker using a Bayesian star identification approach, developed by the University at Buffalo Nanosatellite Lab.
why_it_matters: Full camera-to-attitude pipeline with calibration, proven on small-satellite hardware.
hackathon_notes: Calibration step needed for your camera; budget a few hours.

name: LOST
summary: Open-source star tracker (C++) covering centroiding, star identification and attitude estimation, from the UW CubeSat team.
why_it_matters: Compiled, modular alternative for embedded targets.
hackathon_notes: Build with make; includes test images.

name: NASA COTS Star Tracker
summary: NASA software for building a star tracker from commercial off-the-shelf cameras, including calibration and attitude solution.
why_it_matters: Directly aimed at cheap COTS cameras - the hardware a hackathon team will have.
hackathon_notes: Follow its calibration workflow with a phone or Pi camera.

name: Deep learning celestial navigation
summary: Exploratory project on automating celestial navigation with deep learning and edge inference on synthetic sky images.
why_it_matters: Shows a learning-based route from sky images to position.
hackathon_notes: Concept reference.

name: celestial-navigation toolkit
summary: Python toolkit for classic celestial navigation sight reduction, usable offline on a phone.
why_it_matters: Ground-truth math for turning star/sun sightings into a position.
hackathon_notes: Pair with a star tracker output to compute position.

name: ccompass
summary: Header-only C library for processing sky polarization images to support heading estimation; successor to compyss.
why_it_matters: Polarization compass gives heading without magnetometers or GNSS, robust to magnetic disturbance.
hackathon_notes: Needs a polarization camera (or simulated images).

name: Starlink LEO-PNT
summary: Passive positioning using Starlink downlink signals as signals of opportunity: SDR capture, blind OFDM analysis, Doppler extraction, TDOA/FDOA solver and EKF with TLE-based orbits.
why_it_matters: One of the very few open end-to-end attempts at Starlink-based PNT, a hot GNSS-alternative topic.
hackathon_notes: Needs an SDR that covers Ku-band via LNB, or use the simulation path with TLEs. Treat claims as unverified.

name: LEO SoOP positioning thesis (Voska)
summary: Diploma thesis materials on signals-of-opportunity positioning from LEO satellites using Doppler shift and TLE-based orbits.
why_it_matters: Readable derivation plus code for Doppler positioning from LEO constellations.
hackathon_notes: Use as the math reference for a Doppler-positioning simulator.

name: LEO-SPINE
summary: Open toolkit for LEO/MEO/GEO constellation simulation and single/multi-satellite positioning.
why_it_matters: Lets a team simulate LEO-based positioning geometry and accuracy without hardware.
hackathon_notes: Browser-friendly; good for visualizing LEO coverage in a pitch.

name: GraphGNSSLib LEO
summary: Factor-graph positioning combining GNSS and LEO satellite measurements, extending GraphGNSSLib.
why_it_matters: Shows how LEO observations slot into a factor graph alongside degraded GNSS.
hackathon_notes: C/ROS build; reference.

name: A Tutorial on 5G Positioning (code)
summary: MATLAB simulation code accompanying an IEEE tutorial on 5G positioning (timing, angle and multi-cell methods).
why_it_matters: Cellular positioning is a fallback PNT source; this is a didactic, runnable starting point.
hackathon_notes: MATLAB needed (Octave may partly work).

name: KiwiSDR
summary: Web-accessible shortwave SDR receiver (10 kHz - 30 MHz) with built-in software GPS and a Loran-C/eLoran monitor extension.
why_it_matters: Public KiwiSDR network offers remote access to LF signals for eLoran/Loran experiments without owning hardware.
hackathon_notes: Use public KiwiSDR receivers to look at LF navigation signals; not a positioning solver.
